description: Loads Governed SDD documents when the phase that needs them begins, points agents to the bounded ADR, specification, and queue readers, and aligns the Governed lifecycle text with the closure design and the CLI. Also restructures inline markers into standalone blocks and adds the worktree-lifecycle and remote-branch-cleanup capabilities. A Resume directive starts with `meridian worktree prepare --resume`, which accepts the task's existing dirty worktree. The execution-evidence profile also gains the long-command-waits block: a long command is started with a wait that covers its expected duration and polled at most once, and the full suite runs once after the last code change.
delta: Each routed implementation, review, and remediation procedure gains a phase-reads block that states, per document, whether it is read at start or at the phase that needs it, and a bounded-context-readers block that directs ADR and specification reads through meridian context authority and meridian adr show and queue reads through the queue briefing. The status policy gains a phase-reads block and its minimal-read-only-status block names the briefing and the bounded ADR readers. No acceptance criterion, gate, role, or review rule is removed or relaxed; only the time at which a document is read and the way ADRs are read change. The Governed lifecycle text is also aligned with the closure design and the CLI: task branches never edit the queue, queue archive, or plan, and the task record carries IN_PROGRESS, READY_FOR_REVIEW, and CHANGES_REQUESTED while integrate stage applies the queue status; the task branch is the branch value returned by meridian worktree prepare; a task-branch push happens only to obtain T1_CI, at most once per review attempt, never by the reviewer, and not at all without CI; locations and the reviewer author are resolved by meridian locations and meridian project show --field reviewer-author instead of literal paths and placeholders, and the reviewer identity rule lives in one block; Accept appends an owner APPROVE attempt, sets the task record to ACCEPTED, and continues at C6 without a manual merge; a spike integrates only its deliverable; the reviewer verifies the absolute path resolved at runtime from the recorded handoff_worktree; the task-worktree-boundary block states that only the router read set precedes prepare; and code-organization no longer says the project module map is kept out of its own repository, only out of the managed block. Lean Delivery's git-workflow block carries the branch-name and push rules only. Both PROJECT_WORKFLOW.md templates drop the unread Project integration smoke command line: an untouched line is removed by the three-way merge and a customized line is kept or reported as a conflict, never dropped silently, and its command belongs in .meridian/candidate-validation.json, the only candidate-validation declaration. The capability versions listed in capabilityVersions are keyed per workflow mode. Inline markers inside prose are restructured into standalone blocks: docs/CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT.md becomes one code-review-prompt v1 block that applies a project's own '## Project review checklist' section after it, validation-scoping v2 (the implementation procedure's block becomes complete standalone sentences; the context policy and Lean workflow blocks keep their text under the new version) and the context policy's read-guard block (v2, in both modes) become complete standalone sentences, docs/WORKTREE_LIFECYCLE.md is a whole-file worktree-lifecycle v1 block in both modes, the pull request policy's remote task-branch cleanup section is a remote-branch-cleanup v1 block without the duplicated reviewer identity rule, and audit-prompt v3 runs a project's '## Project-specific checks' section after the block. An upgrade that cannot merge cleanly around the retired inline markers preserves the current file in an adjacent collision-safe backup and carries the project's own level-2 sections after the new block. The worktree boundary and lifecycle text add that a Resume directive runs `prepare --resume`, that `--resume` is allowed only for that directive, that `dirty-worktree` is then the only tolerated `check` error, and that the agent reads `git status` and the diff before continuing; no existing gate is relaxed. docs/EXECUTION_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.md adds a long-command-waits v1 block after the foreground-timeout rule, in both modes; it states the wait-once rule for long commands, the Codex session semantics, and that the full suite runs once after the last code change without changing the declared candidate validation. The foreground-timeout rule is unchanged.
verification: a clean Governed SDD upgrade installs phase-reads v1 and bounded-context-readers v1 in the three role procedures and minimal-read-only-status v2 in the context policy while preserving consumer-owned text
meridian context size reports each deferred document separately and leaves it out of the startup total
marker baselines record the new and bumped capability versions for all managed paths

a clean Governed SDD upgrade installs the bumped lifecycle blocks and a Lean upgrade installs git-workflow v9 while preserving consumer-owned text, including a '## Project module map' section after the code-organization block

python3 scripts/check_repository.py rejects a managed block that says a role edits a queue row, a Governed block that names a literal queue, review, or handoff location outside execution-assets, a placeholder identity, and a second place that states the reviewer identity rule
python3 scripts/check_repository.py and python3 -m unittest discover -s tests pass

docs/CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT.md carries one code-review-prompt v1 block and none of the retired task-worktree-review v4, manual-verification-review-check v1, or ci-verified-validation v1 inline markers; the PULL_REQUEST_POLICY.md and COMPLETION_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md ci-verified-validation v1 blocks are unchanged

an upgrade of a project whose retired inline markers sit inside edited prose writes the pre-upgrade file to an adjacent .meridian-pre-restructure.bak backup, reports it, and keeps the project's own level-2 sections after the new block
meridian audit reports a FAIL row for a markerless managed copy whose digest differs from managedFiles and never for project text outside the capability blocks of a marker-bearing file
meridian profile bootstrap governed-sdd-consumer and lean-delivery-consumer declare installation evidence on a legacy v2 manifest and leave host activation UNVERIFIED

an upgrade whose three-way merge conflicts inside docs/WORKTREE_LIFECYCLE.md or the pull request policy's remote task-branch cleanup section reports a conflict instead of appending a duplicate worktree-lifecycle or remote-branch-cleanup block

a Lean Delivery upgrade installs bounded-worktree-lifecycle v4 and a Governed SDD upgrade installs task-worktree-boundary v8, each stating that `meridian worktree prepare --resume` is allowed only for a Resume directive; both modes install worktree-lifecycle v2
an upgrade adds exactly one long-command-waits v1 block to a customized docs/EXECUTION_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.md in both workflow modes and leaves the surrounding project text unchanged
